report:
**Conclusion: The claim is well-supported by evidence — it is not false.** Multiple large studies consistently show hands-only (compression-only) CPR is associated with better survival than no bystander CPR at all.

**Evidence:**

1. **Randomized controlled trials of dispatcher-assisted CPR** directly compared compression-only CPR to standard CPR (with rescue breaths) in witnessed arrests. A meta-analysis of these RCTs found chest-compression-only CPR was associated with *improved* survival (14% vs. 12%) compared to standard CPR — and both dramatically outperform no CPR (https://www.ems1.com/research-monitor/articles/for-dispatcher-assisted-cpr-compression-only-may-be-best-NSEdFSCAsRKQZeIT/).

2. **Japan's nationwide OHCA registry**, one of the largest population-based datasets on this topic, found that bystander-initiated compression-only CPR was linked to significantly better neurological survival outcomes than no bystander CPR, and that population-wide dissemination of compression-only CPR increased survival with favorable neurological outcomes (https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.112.109504; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26048093/).

3. Data from a related large nationwide registry also showed bystander CPR (both conventional and compression-only) is associated with higher survival than no bystander CPR, including in pediatric arrests (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0140673610600645).

4. A JAMA study cited by Wikipedia found bystanders using hands-only CPR boosted survival to 34%, versus 18% for those receiving conventional CPR or no CPR at all (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiopulmonary_resuscitation).

**Caveat:** Some nuance exists — conventional CPR with rescue breathing appears superior for prolonged arrests, non-cardiac causes, and pediatric arrests specifically, but for the general adult population with witnessed sudden cardiac arrest, hands-only CPR performs at least as well as, and often better than, conventional CPR, and both are clearly superior to no CPR. The claim as stated is accurate.
